title: Projects
text:
2026


 



AI-Leading Teacher Training Program  · 2026


Participated in the 2026 AI-Leading Teacher Training Program, a nationwide blended (online and in-person) professional development program for elementary and secondary teachers. The program focused on using AI and digital technologies in teaching and learning, with intensive tracks organized by teacher level and subject. Responsible for developing the training materials for the secondary social studies track, including AI-based lesson design and classroom activities.


Organized by: Korea Education and Research Information Service (한국교육학술정보원)  Ministry of Education (교육부)





 



Micro-Degree Winter Professional Development Program  · 2026


Participated in a collaborative winter professional development program jointly organized by the Seoul National University Learning Sciences Institute and the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education. The program focused on designing and developing interactive dashboards that can be directly implemented in classroom instruction.


Organized by: Seoul National University Learning Sciences Institute (서울대학교 학습과학연구소)  Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education (서울특별시교육청)

Welcoming Our New Undergraduate Research Intern 👨🏻‍💻📚
We are pleased to welcome a new undergraduate research intern who will be joining the SDS Lab for the semester.
Our new intern is Yangseon Kim, a student from the Class of 2024 in the Department of Geography Education at Seoul National University. He currently serves as the president of the undergraduate GIS academic society and has demonstrated diligence in a wide range of activities.
We are delighted to have him join our lab and look forward to working and learning together throughout the semester.
Welcome to the GIS Lab, Yangseon!

At the 2025 Korean Geography Conference held on June 27–28, our lab’s master’s degree candidate, Hyemin, presented her thesis titled “Regionalization of the Seoul Metropolitan Area Using Graph Transformer-Based Representation Learning and Spatially Constrained Clustering.” Congratulations to her, and we wish her all the best after graduation!

title: New Publication in Geographical Analysis: Introducing ML-SAS
section: New Publication in Geographical Analysis: Introducing ML-SAS
text:
New Publication in Geographical Analysis: Introducing ML-SAS
We are pleased to announce that Woohyung Kim and Professor Sang-Il Lee have published a paper in the international journal Geographical Analysis!
Their paper, titled “ML-SAS: A Machine-Learning-Based Spatial Autocorrelation Statistic for Mixed-Type Data,” proposes a novel spatial autocorrelation statistic that integrates machine learning with spatial statistical analysis. By utilizing unsupervised random forests, the proposed method enables the joint analysis of continuous and categorical variables, offering a new approach to identifying complex spatial patterns. Through simulation experiments and an empirical application to Dutch municipalities, the study demonstrates the potential of ML-SAS for analyzing multivariate spatial relationships.
We sincerely applaud their hard work and dedication throughout the research process. Congratulations once again to both authors on this wonderful achievement!
Reference
Kim, W., and S.-I. Lee. 2026. “ML-SAS: A Machine-Learning-Based Spatial Autocorrelation Statistic for Mixed-Type Data.” Geographical Analysis 58, no. 4: e70062.

To celebrate the end of the midterm exam for ‘Spatial Data Analysis and Geography Education (Spatial Interaction Data Analysis)’, our lab gathered for a well-deserved dinner together.
